rows.stem: The name and formula of third member of homologous series of alkyne is :
rows.solution:
Alkynes have the general formula \(\mathrm{C_nH_{2n-2}}\). The first member is ethyne, \(\mathrm{C_2H_2}\), the second is propyne, \(\mathrm{C_3H_4}\), and the third is butyne, \(\mathrm{C_4H_6}\) (n = 4 gives \(2 \times 4 - 2 = 6\) hydrogen atoms). \(\mathrm{C_3H_6}\) and \(\mathrm{C_4H_8}\) are alkenes.

This is option (D) Butyne \(\mathrm{C_4H_6}\).

rows.stem: Which one of the following statements is **NOT** true ?

options.label: A
options.text: DNA carries the information for inheritance of features from parents to the next generation.

options.label: B
options.text: DNA is the information source for making proteins.

options.label: C
options.text: Change in the information leads to different proteins.

options.label: D
options.text: Features will remain the same even if the protein changes.

rows.solution:
DNA in the cell nucleus is the information source for making proteins, and it carries this information from parents to the next generation. If the information changes, a different protein is made, and a different protein changes the feature it controls. For example, an efficient enzyme makes enough growth hormone for a tall plant, while a less efficient form of the enzyme gives a short plant. So the first three statements are true, and the claim that features stay the same when the protein changes is false.

This is option (D) Features will remain the same even if the protein changes.

rows.stem: A ray of light falls making an angle of incidence \(\theta\) on the surface of a glass slab. Draw a labelled ray diagram to show its path. Also mark lateral displacement on it.
rows.solution:
When a ray of light passes obliquely through a rectangular glass slab, it bends towards the normal on entering the glass and away from the normal on leaving it. The emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray but shifted sideways.

Ray diagram: draw the rectangular glass slab ABCD, with air on both sides. Let the incident ray EO strike the upper face AB at O, making the angle of incidence \(\theta\) with the normal NN' drawn at O. Inside the slab the refracted ray OO' bends towards the normal (angle of refraction \(r < \theta\)) and meets the lower face CD at O'. At O' draw another normal; the emergent ray O'H bends away from this normal, and the angle of emergence equals \(\theta\), so O'H is parallel to EO. Produce the incident ray EO straight on through the slab as a dotted line. The perpendicular distance between this dotted line and the emergent ray O'H is the lateral displacement: mark it with a short perpendicular line between the two and label it "lateral displacement". Put arrows on the rays.

rows.subtopic: Human Brain and Protection of Nervous Tissue
rows.stem: In which region of the brain is (i) medulla and (ii) cerebrum located ? State one function of each.
rows.solution:
(i) The medulla is located in the hind-brain. It controls involuntary actions such as blood pressure, salivation and vomiting.

(ii) The cerebrum is located in the fore-brain. It is the main thinking part of the brain and is responsible for thinking, intelligence and memory. (Any other correct function of each is also accepted.)

rows.stem: Name a hormone that promotes the growth of tendrils and explain how they help a pea plant to climb up other plants.
rows.solution:
Auxin promotes the growth of tendrils.

When the tendril of a pea plant comes in contact with a support, the part of the tendril in contact with the object does not grow as rapidly as the part of the tendril away from it. The faster growth on the far side makes the tendril circle around the object and cling to it, so the pea plant climbs up the support.

rows.stem: Mention the pathway of urine in our body starting from the organ of its formation to its excretion. What will happen if the tubular part of the nephron does not work properly?
rows.solution:
Urine is formed in the kidneys and flows out as follows:

Kidney \(\rightarrow\) ureter \(\rightarrow\) urinary bladder \(\rightarrow\) urethra

From the urinary bladder it is passed out through the urethra.

If the tubular part of the nephron does not work properly, the selective reabsorption of useful substances such as glucose, amino acids, salts and a major amount of water will not take place. These substances will be lost in the urine.

rows.stem:
Translate the following statements into chemical equations and then balance them :

(i) Solution of barium chloride and aluminium sulphate in water react to give insoluble barium sulphate and the solution of aluminium chloride.

(ii) Aluminium metal reacts with steam to give aluminium oxide and hydrogen gas.
rows.solution:
(i) Barium chloride and aluminium sulphate exchange ions to give a white precipitate of barium sulphate, leaving aluminium chloride in solution:

\(\mathrm{3BaCl_2(aq) + Al_2(SO_4)_3(aq) \rightarrow 3BaSO_4(s) + 2AlCl_3(aq)}\)

Check: Ba 3 = 3; Cl 6 = 6; Al 2 = 2; S 3 = 3; O 12 = 12.

(ii) Aluminium reacts with steam to form aluminium oxide and hydrogen gas:

\(\mathrm{2Al(s) + 3H_2O(g) \rightarrow Al_2O_3(s) + 3H_2(g)}\)

Check: Al 2 = 2; H 6 = 6; O 3 = 3.

rows.stem:
In the context of the statement “chlorophyll is necessary for photosynthesis” answer the following questions :

(i) What are variegated leaves? Give an example.

(ii) When leaf is boiled in alcohol, what happens to the colour of the leaf and the colour of the solution ?

(iii) In what form is the carbohydrate produced, stored in the plant? Why is chlorophyll necessary for photosynthesis ?
rows.solution:
(i) Variegated leaves are leaves that have green patches (containing chlorophyll) and non-green patches (white or yellow, without chlorophyll). Croton and money plant have variegated leaves.

(ii) When the leaf is boiled in alcohol, the chlorophyll dissolves in the alcohol. So the leaf becomes colourless (pale), and the alcohol solution turns green.

(iii) The carbohydrate produced in photosynthesis is stored in the plant in the form of starch.

Chlorophyll is necessary because it absorbs the energy of sunlight, which is the energy used to make carbohydrates from carbon dioxide and water. When a variegated leaf is tested with iodine, only the parts that were green turn blue-black, showing that starch is made only where chlorophyll is present.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem:
A narrow beam, PQ of white light is passing through a glass prism ABC as shown in the diagram.

Draw a ray diagram to show the emergent beam as it falls on the screen DE. Also write the phenomenon involved and its cause. Using the second law of refraction state which colour of light must have the highest value of refractive index amongst seven visible colours of light. Justify your answer.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the set-up the student must complete exists only in the drawing: a triangular glass prism ABC (apex A at the top, base BC), a ray from P striking face AB at Q, and a vertical screen DE standing to the right of the prism beyond C. The emergent beam is to be drawn onto this figure. Page idx 16.
rows.solution:
Ray diagram: on the given figure, the ray PQ enters the prism at Q on face AB and bends towards the normal. Inside the prism it splits into a band of colours that spread out as they travel to face AC. At face AC each colour bends away from the normal and emerges, and the emergent beam spreads out into a spectrum on the screen DE. Red is deviated the least, so it reaches the screen nearest D (at the top); violet is deviated the most, so it reaches the screen nearest E (at the bottom). Label the colours on the screen from top to bottom as red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet (R, O, Y, G, B, I, V), and put arrows on the rays.

Phenomenon: dispersion of white light, the splitting of white light into its seven component colours.

Cause: the different colours of white light bend through different angles with respect to the incident ray as they pass through the prism, because light of different colours (different wavelengths) travels at different speeds in glass.

By the second law of refraction (Snell's law), for light of a given colour and a given pair of media,

\(\dfrac{\sin i}{\sin r} = n\), a constant (the refractive index).

All seven colours have the same angle of incidence at Q. Violet bends the most, so its angle of refraction r is the smallest, and \(\sin r\) is the smallest. With the same \(\sin i\), the ratio \(\dfrac{\sin i}{\sin r}\) is then the largest for violet. So violet light has the highest refractive index of the seven colours.

rows.stem:
(i) Name two safety measures commonly used in electric circuits and appliances.

(ii) The power rating of an electric oven is 220 V; 2 kW. If it is used in a domestic electric circuit of current rating of 5A, what result do you expect ? Justify your answer with necessary calculations.
rows.solution:
(i) Any two: an electric fuse, and earthing of metallic appliances through an earth wire. (A miniature circuit breaker is also used in place of a fuse.)

(ii) The current drawn by the oven is

\(I = \dfrac{P}{V} = \dfrac{2000\ \text{W}}{220\ \text{V}} = 9.09\) A.

This is more than the current rating of the circuit, since \(9.09\) A \(> 5\) A. The circuit is overloaded, so the fuse wire in it will melt and break the circuit, and the oven will stop working. The oven cannot be used safely on this circuit.

rows.stem:
(i) Define the term functional group. Identify the functional groups present in the following carbon compounds :

(I) \(\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3}\)

(II) \(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2COOH}\)

(ii) What happens when ethanol reacts with acidified potassium dichromate solution ? Write chemical equation for the reaction. Why is this reaction considered an oxidation reaction ?

(iii) Write chemical equation for the reaction of ethanoic acid with sodium hydroxide.
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - compounds (I) and (II) are printed as full displayed structural formulas: (I) three carbons in a chain, the middle one double-bonded to O and each end carbon carrying three H; (II) three carbons in a chain, the first carrying three H, the second two H, the third carrying OH and double-bonded to O. The stem gives the same two compounds as condensed formulas, so it is answerable without the drawing. Page idx 16.
rows.solution:
(i) A functional group is an atom (a heteroatom) or a group of atoms attached to the carbon chain of a compound, which gives the compound its specific (characteristic) chemical properties.

(I) \(\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3}\) contains the ketone group, \(\mathrm{>C{=}O}\) (it is propanone).

(II) \(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2COOH}\) contains the carboxylic acid group, \(\mathrm{-COOH}\) (it is propanoic acid).

(ii) When ethanol is heated with acidified potassium dichromate solution, it is oxidised to ethanoic acid. The orange colour of the dichromate solution turns green.

\(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH \xrightarrow{\text{acidified } K_2Cr_2O_7,\ \text{heat}} CH_3COOH}\)

It is an oxidation reaction because oxygen is added to ethanol (and hydrogen is removed from it) as it is converted to ethanoic acid. Acidified potassium dichromate is the oxidising agent that supplies the oxygen.

(iii) Ethanoic acid reacts with sodium hydroxide to give sodium ethanoate (sodium acetate) and water:

\(\mathrm{CH_3COOH + NaOH \rightarrow CH_3COONa + H_2O}\)

rows.stem:
(i) Describe method of preparation of soap giving chemical equation for the reaction involved.

(ii) Explain with diagram the mechanism of the cleansing action of soaps.
rows.solution:
(i) Soap is prepared by heating an ester, an animal fat or vegetable oil, with a base such as sodium hydroxide solution. The ester is converted back into the alcohol and the sodium salt of the carboxylic acid. This reaction is called saponification. Common salt is then added to the mixture, and the soap separates out as a solid.

\(\mathrm{CH_3COOC_2H_5 + NaOH \rightarrow CH_3COONa + C_2H_5OH}\)

(ethyl ethanoate gives sodium ethanoate and ethanol)

A fat or oil is an ester of long-chain fatty acids with glycerol, so with it the products are the sodium salt of a long-chain fatty acid, which is soap, and glycerol. For example,

\(\mathrm{(C_{17}H_{35}COO)_3C_3H_5 + 3NaOH \rightarrow 3C_{17}H_{35}COONa + C_3H_5(OH)_3}\)

(ii) A soap molecule has two ends with different properties: an ionic end (\(\mathrm{-COO^-Na^+}\)), which is hydrophilic and dissolves in water, and a long hydrocarbon chain, which is hydrophobic and dissolves in oil. Most dirt is oily.

When soap is dissolved in water and applied to oily dirt, the hydrocarbon tails of many soap molecules dissolve in the oil droplet, while the ionic ends stay outside, facing the water. The molecules arrange themselves in a cluster around the droplet, called a micelle, with the oily dirt trapped at its centre. The micelles stay suspended in the water as an emulsion and do not come together, because their ionic outer surfaces repel one another. When the cloth is rinsed with water, the micelles carrying the oily dirt are washed away, and the cloth is cleaned.

Diagram: draw an oil droplet at the centre with many soap molecules arranged radially around it, each with its hydrocarbon tail (a zig-zag line) pointing into the droplet and its ionic head (a small circle, with \(\mathrm{Na^+}\)) pointing outwards into the water. Label the oil droplet, the hydrocarbon tail, the ionic head and the micelle.
